minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  March 11, 2025

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
March 11, 2025, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  Absent: None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk
  Louis A. Atwell  City Manager
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney
  Destinee Wesley  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  ******************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:04 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Angela Allen  City Treasurer/Treasurer
  Louis A. Atwell  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Destinee Wesley  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority Members on
any item on the Agendas.

There was no response.
 March 11, 2025

142.9  PAYMENT WARRANTS AND BILLS – RECEIVED AND FILED. The demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated March 7, 2025,
  in the amount of $7,162,881.09, and dated March 6, 2025, in the amount of $43,233.30, are
  hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are received
  and filed.

  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts ordered the
  Warrants and Bills received and filed.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims in accordance with Government Code, Section 913:
  1. David Martin for alleged property damage on September 27, 2024; Sewer line
  hydrojetting (Contractor: Mattucci Plumbing).
  2. Patrina Miller for alleged property damage on September 27, 2024; Sewer line
  hydrojetting (Contractor: Mattucci Plumbing).
  3. Ciennese J. Mones Pineda for alleged property damage on February 16, 2025; Tire
  and rims; lifted manhole (vault located outside City limits – owned by LADWP).
  B. Reject Insufficient Claims in accordance with Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Charter Communications for alleged property damage on January 28, 2024; No 811
  dig ticket notice (location is outside of Inglewood city limit).
  2. Javier Yanez for alleged personal injury on December 19, 2024; Pothole.
  C. Return Late Claim in accordance with Government Code, Section 911.2:
  1. Charter Communications for alleged property damage on January 28, 2024; No 811
  dig ticket notice (location is outside of Inglewood City limit).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 and A-3; 2) Reject Insufficient
  Claims listed as B-1 and B-2; and 3) Return Late Claim listed as C-1.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  PRESENTATION OF THE FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 FIRST QUARTER REVIEW
  REPORT RECEIVED AND FILED. Staff report dated March 11, 2025, presenting the
  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 First Quarter Review Report.

  Mayor Butts ordered the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 First Quarter Review Report received and
  filed.

131.8  PUBLIC HEARING SET – DRAFT SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN. Staff report dated March 11,
  2025, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to receiver public input in the
  Draft Substantial Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Annual Action Plan to
  reallocate U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Community Development
  Block Grant (CDBG) – Coronavirus (CV) funds.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing to be set for March 25, 2025, at the hour of 2:00p.m.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, attended Councilwoman
  Faulk’s Women as We Worship Benefit Concert, as well as Assemblymember Tina
  McKinnor’s Emergency Preparedness event. The City Clerk also reminded residents that
  the 4th Annual Women’s Rock event will be held on May 3, 2025. Lastly, the City Clerk
  requested that the meeting be closed in honor of Mrs. Evelyn Alexander, a valued Inglewood
  resident and former City of Inglewood employee.

  Council Woman Faulk left the Dias at the hour of 2:08pm.

  *************

  2
 March 11, 2025

  Council Woman Faulk returned to the Dias at the hour of 2:09pm.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Channel Webber, a Public Information Officer for the Small Business Administration,
  shared that the SBA offers a variety of loans to assist with both natural and man-made
  disasters.

  Charlen Sanders expressed her gratitude to Assembly Member McKinnor for organizing
  the disaster preparedness event and thanked Jeffrey Givens and Jerry Tucker for delivering
  the leftover items to those in need, particularly the homeless.

  Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 2:25 p.m. for Closed Session Item No.
  CS-1.

  ******************

  Mayor Butts reconvened the City Council Meeting at the hour of 4:17pm.

  CLOSED SESSION – NAME OF AGENCY NEGOTIATORS – NAME OF
  ORGANIZATIONS REPRESENTING EMPLOYEES. Closed Session – Confidential
  – Attorney/Client Privileged; Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54957.6; Name of Agency Negotiators: Jose O. Cortes, Assistant City
  Manager, and Sylvia L. Fernandez, Human Resources Director; Name of Organizations
  Representing Employees: Inglewood Police Officers Association (IPOA); and Inglewood
  Police Management Association (IPMA).

  Discussion Held; Feedback provided and No final action taken.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Eleven Alexander and Auvrill Culley at the hour of 4:20 p.m.

  Approved this 15th day of April, 2025.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
